newsitem.title: CHINA: China personal income tax revenue soaring.
newsitem.headline: China personal income tax revenue soaring.

text.p: China's personal income tax revenue for the first half soared 42.5 percent from a year ago to 12.34 billion yuan, the China Daily said on Thursday.

Total revenue for the year was expected to exceed 24 billion yuan, lifting the ratio of personal income tax to industrial and commercial tax to 3.45 percent from last year's 3.0 percent, it said quoting Ye Lin'er, deputy division chief of the Income Taxation Department of the State Taxation Administration.
He attributed the higher tax collection to rising incomes and tougher policing of tax evasion.
Last year, personal income revenue rose a year-on-year 46.9 percent to 19.3 billion yuan.

China's customs collected 44.72 billion yuan of taxes in the first half, up 3.84 billion yuan, or 9.4 percent compared with the previous year, the China Daily said quoting the General Customs Administration.

In the first six months, China levied import duties worth 16.85 billion yuan, up 1.3 percent. Import taxes -- value-added tax and consumption duties -- totalled 27.87 billion yuan, a jump of 15 percent, it said.
